agencies.name: Pollution Control Department (PCD), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
agencies.role: Sets Thailand's air quality index criteria and runs national monitoring. Leads cooperation with neighbours on transboundary haze data.

nationalIndex.name: Air Quality Index (Thailand)
nationalIndex.description: PCD's index uses five colour levels (blue, green, yellow, orange, red). From 1 June 2023 the PM2.5 threshold was lowered from 50 to 37.5 µg/m³ and the red level from 91 to 75.1 µg/m³, which the government says follows WHO guidelines and interim targets.

monitoring.text: In May 2026 PCD agreed with Myanmar's Environmental Conservation Department to integrate monitoring platforms and share air pollution data, and to help Myanmar build online haze reporting.

seasonalPattern.text: ASMC's alerts for the northern ASEAN and Mekong region typically run from about December to May.
From late March 2024 Chiang Mai's air quality was among the world's worst, with officials counting about 500 hotspots in Chiang Mai in April, Global Voices reported.

healthContext.text: Global Voices reported that over 30,000 people in Chiang Mai were treated for PM2.5-related illness in the first quarter of 2024.

policy.text: Tighter PM2.5 thresholds for the national AQI took effect.
